messages.author: 4e629a130193773b
messages.subject: Difficulty and guessing model
parts:
Dear mirt-community,

I try to estimate a Difficulty and guessing model, that means like a 3PL-model but with a fixed slope.
To be sure that everything works fine with the model I first estimated it with the great package "sirt" from Alexander Robitzsch who helped me a lot.

Because I made the experience that sometimes different packages estimate the models different I wanted to try the same thing with mirt.
Unfortunately there are quite huge differences.

I would appreciate it a lot, if anybody could help me with this.
Below is a syntax with a simulated dataset.

Best

Petra


library(mirt)
library(sirt)
library(TAM)
#***
# (1) simulate data
set.seed(785)
library(mvtnorm)
N <- 500
N <- 3000
theta <- mvtnorm::rmvnorm( N,mean=c(0,0), sigma=matrix( c(1.45,.5,.5,1.7) , 2 ,
                                                        2 ))
theta[,2] <- theta[,1]
I <- 10
# 10 items load on the first dimension
p1 <- stats::plogis( outer( theta[,1] , seq( -2 , 2 , len=I ) , "-" ) )
resp1 <- 1 * ( p1 > matrix( stats::runif( N*I ) , nrow=N , ncol=I ) )
# 10 items load on the second dimension
p1 <- stats::plogis( outer( theta[,2] , seq( -2 , 2 , len=I ) , "-" ) )
resp2 <- 1 * ( p1 > matrix( stats::runif( N*I ) , nrow=N , ncol=I ) )
#Combine the two sets of items into one response matrix
resp_t <- cbind(resp1,resp2)
colnames(resp) <- paste("I" , 1:(2*I), sep="")
dat <- resp_t
#**** Schaetzung in sirt
mod1 <- sirt::rasch.mml2( dat , est.c = 1:20  , theta.k = seq(-6,6,len=21) )
summary(mod1)

#**** Schaetzung in mirt
modelxDAT <- "F = 1-20"
pars <- mirt(dat, itemtype='3PL',modelxDAT, pars = 'values')
pars$est[which(pars$name == 'a1')] <- FALSE
pars$value[which(pars$name == 'a1')] <- 1
mod3 <- mirt(dat, itemtype='3PL',modelxDAT, pars = pars)
coef(mod3)
modelxDAT <- "F = 1-20"

messages.subject: Re: Difficulty and guessing model
parts:
There are 41 estimated parameters in the sirt model, while only 40 for mirt. I suspect it's because the latent variance parameter has been estimated. So, either freely estimate this parameter, or (equivalently) estimate all the slope parameters subject to the constrain that they are all equal. Like so:

model <- 'F = 1-20
               CONSTRAIN = (1-20, a1)'
mod3 <- mirt(dat, model, itemtype = '3PL')

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Difficulty and guessing model
parts:
On Thu, Nov 24, 2016 at 7:41 PM, <petraw...@gmail.com> wrote:
Thank you very much for the quick response!
If it´s okay two more question:
1) Where do you think come the - now quite small - differences in the estimates (mirt <-> sirt)

In very small technical choices between the package code, too many to list without being an expert in both. I imagine other programs like Mplus will be the same; it's the nature of software development.
2) Is ist possible to use the same "3PL-model with fixed slope" for an EFA or the bifactor-model of mirt.
bifactor sure, EFA no. The purpose of EFA is to do rotation post-estimation, so constraining slopes doesn't make a lot of sense.

Thanks in advance,
best

Petra
